label: input token w at early original positions (t=2-4)
explanation: Token-specific, position-gated feature: fires only when the input is the letter w during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, and essentially only at positions t=1-5, with nearly all mass at t=2-4. 100% of activations are on input w. Magnitude grows with position from t=1 (weak, fires on only about a third of w-at-t=1 cases, low magnitude) to a peak at t=3 (about 45% of mass), then falls off: weak at t=5, and essentially never at t>=6 or t=0. It is somewhat weaker on repeat occurrences of w. Top activations (around 1.5-1.65) are w at t=3 that often come after earlier r/m tokens, but conditioning on r gives no useful predicate. Does NOT fire on the delimiter, on the copy phase (even when w is output or fed back as input; about 100 tiny exceptions), or on any other token. Including t=1 raises mass recall to 0.99 but lowers precision (F1 0.88 vs 0.89).

issues: Core claims check out on the dev profile. Every activation is on in_tok w (100% of mass). Original phase holds 0.999 of the mass, the delimiter 0, and the copy phase only 103 steps (0.001). By position the mass is t=1 0.037, t=2 0.324, t=3 0.450, t=4 0.184, t=5 0.005, with t=0 and t>=6 at zero apart from the 62 copy-phase steps at t=7. Test scores reproduce: P 0.932, R 0.850, F1 0.889, mass recall 0.957.

Precision is uneven across the predicate's own positions. It is 0.994 at t=2 and 0.991 at t=3 but only 0.790 at t=4, so about 21% of w's at t=4 are inactive. Prior digits lower it a little (0.84 with no digits vs 0.72 with 2 or more), but I found no crisp class behind it, so I treat it as graded weakening rather than a counterexample class.

The claim that it is 'a bit weaker on repeated w's' is not supported. At t=2-4, a repeated w (in_first==0) has precision 0.926 against 0.932 overall, and its mass recall to recall ratio is about 1.05, which is no weaker. Mass per active step is also flat across in_count values. This is a minor overclaim.

There is a small systematic pattern at t=1 that the explanation describes only as 'about a third'. A w at t=1 fires 74% of the time after a digit but only 35% after a letter. Adding (t==1 & previous token is a digit) raises test F1 from 0.889 to 0.903. This is a minor refinement on about 4% of the mass.

Missed activations are low-magnitude: coverage in the lowest activation quartile is 0.46, against 0.94 or higher in the other quartiles. Most misses are weak t=1 and t=5 w's, and the false positives are mostly t=4 w's, so I see no hidden token or history class.
